would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: verifier/registration-property.log:1 — "FAIL case 3: a REPLAYED emit against a run with events but no registry row did not register it — the open happens after the idempotency early-return"; mechanism at artefacts/src/omegahive/gateway/gateway.py:101-113 (early `return Accepted(existing)` at line 104 precedes `self._store.open_run()` at line 113).
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The idempotent open is placed after the idempotency early-return, so a replayed emit against a run that has events but no registry row still leaves it unregistered — exactly the state the durable `omegahive` run is in.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: The order's item 2 rests on `omegahive` entering the registry as a side effect of its next real emit. Every pre-existing run has events and no registry row; if that next emit carries an idempotency key that hits `find_by_key` (a client retry / ack-loss replay, the normal case the key exists for), `Gateway.emit` returns `Accepted(existing)` at step 1 and never reaches `open_run` at step 2a. The run stays unregistered while the shipped runbook now tells the operator the bump is a live signal, so a post-restore operator gets `run not registered` from `bump-generation --run-id omegahive` after being told registration is automatic — the interim 'restart every client' floor is silently back, unannounced, which is the precise failure the order exists to remove. The candidate's report reasons this away with 'its original emit already registered the run' (docs/evidence/2026-07-21-run-registration-result.md, candidate.patch:51-52), which is false for any run whose original emits predate this change.
